The Docker daemon is dead, but three mounts from an interrupted BuildKit operation remain:

- Two overlay mounts under `/var/tmp/agent-sandbox-docker-1000-main/buildkit/`
- One network namespace mount under `/run/user/1000/agent-sandbox-docker-main/exec/netns/`

On activation, `agent-dockerd-runner` runs `rm -rf` before starting Docker. `rm` cannot remove mounted directories, so the script exits before creating the socket. Its exit trap tries the same cleanup again, which explains the duplicate errors.

`ps` shows nothing because mounts can remain after their processes exit. `rm -rf` does not unmount them.

Recover with:

```bash
sudo umount \
  /var/tmp/agent-sandbox-docker-1000-main/buildkit/executor/rlz8j7gchh2a5h4vjac0pijcj/rootfs \
  /var/tmp/agent-sandbox-docker-1000-main/buildkit/containerd-overlayfs/cachemounts/buildkit4147141418 \
  /run/user/1000/agent-sandbox-docker-main/exec/netns/0fb0d03c3492

sudo rm -rf \
  /run/user/1000/agent-sandbox-docker-main \
  /var/tmp/agent-sandbox-docker-1000-main

direnv reload
```

The code bug is in `nix/flake/dev-partition.nix`: startup assumes deleting Docker’s directories also cleans up stale mounts. Cleanup needs to unmount residual BuildKit and network-namespace mounts before calling `rm -rf`.
Put that script in /tmp for the one-off fix and fix this in `nix/flake/dev-partition.nix`.

worktree Docker daemon stops. These mounts make startup cleanup fail
before the new daemon creates its socket.

Keep image data outside the runtime directory. Unmount each stale mount
from the deepest path first, then remove the runtime and data trees.
Use a lazy unmount only when a normal unmount fails.
EOF
git commit -F "$msg"
rm -f "$msg"
